topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and frames how it builds on previously introduced immunological concepts.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition and pattern detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the innate immune system distinguishes pathogens and cellular damage through conserved molecular patterns and strategically localized pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and intracellular signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific pattern recognition receptor families, their downstream signaling cascades, and the inflammasome assembly that processes inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment, cell trafficking, and systemic inflammatory effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells coordinate leukocyte extravasation into tissues, how immune cells traffic through lymphatic vessels, and the clinical risks of uncontrolled systemic inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, the processes of tissue repair, and the causes and functions of chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the complement system.
